# C1 mathematical/source-correctness review

Scope: frozen commit d1ab5554e18b664bf7713b3350042470d691e537 against base b8306d6b9775d34fdbbb4504f639fe98085efd38. Read the mathematical adversary instructions, all four OpenSpec planning artifacts, the recovery state machine, its controller integration and relevant review/adjudication callers, recovery tests, and supervisor guidance. There are no changed Lean declarations or mathematical assumptions.

Findings: 0 blockers, 1 should-fix finding (source/workflow contract consistency, shared with the style lens).

`.claude/skills/run-loop/SKILL.md:214` — should-fix
The supervising protocol unconditionally instructs that the style reviewer closes with `MERGE` / `MERGE AFTER FIXES` / `NEEDS REWORK`, and claims the controller performs the mapping. However, `scripts/loop_recovery.py:142` requires the final line to be exactly `Close: PASS`, `Close: NEEDS_CHANGES`, or another actual controller verdict, and `.claude/agents/mathlib-reviewer.md:71` leaves `<TOKEN>` unspecified while its only enumerated verdict vocabulary remains the legacy one at line 90. A reviewer following that vocabulary can return `Reviewed commit: <sha>` followed by `Close: MERGE`; recording it as `pass` then fails the strict validator. Thus an otherwise successful unattended recovery panel can stall on contradictory executable guidance, the very stale-instruction problem this change promises to remove. Qualify the supervisor's legacy mapping paragraph as non-recovery only, explicitly enumerate recovery style tokens and their semantic mapping in the reviewer instructions, and add a regression/documented transcript showing the recovery style output is accepted unchanged. Do not weaken the strict trailer or have the supervisor rewrite the review.

Reconstructed invariants:

- Reserving a round charges it before review; retrying an incomplete same-commit panel preserves that slot. A changed commit cannot replace an open panel. Each attempt admits at most three allocations.
- Failed, imported, and abandoned partial rounds remain counted. Resume seals the previous attempt before clearing only its active rounds, so archival transfer conserves the aggregate count. Episode and plan-submission bounds and the elapsed deadline independently limit continuation.
- A failed third complete panel transitions to investigation when allowance remains. An accepted research plan is bound to its exact digest and original contract, requires a reviewer distinct from both researcher and implementer, and admits a successor without granting publication.
- Every negative verbatim transcript survives as an indivisible finding. Resume requires the complete finding inventory. A passing successor requires a complete passing same-commit panel and every review's complete resolution-evidence map.
- Publication requires an active, passed objective and an unexpired budget, while the controller additionally binds the exact reviewed head. Registry-owned canonical state and immutable contract checks prevent the supported restart/cache interfaces from replenishing counts.

Verification: independently ran `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_loop_recovery -q`: 24 tests passed. This is focused local verification, not a CI claim. Tested and inspected counterexamples include fourth-round allocation, changing an open panel's commit, incomplete panels, omitted historical findings, self-approved plans, changed contract fields, rejected-plan exhaustion, partial-round abandonment, altered cache state, and historical snapshot mutation.

Limits: semantic adequacy of research evidence and finding resolutions remains an independent reviewer obligation, not a theorem established by nonempty strings or identity labels. This limitation is explicit in the design. No inherited formal findings were supplied for this first implementation panel; the resolution map is `{}`.

# C1 repository-boundary adversarial review

Reviewed the frozen change against its OpenSpec proposal, design, specification,
tasks, repository instructions, reviewer instructions and changed provider/state
callers. No Lean source, ownership, import, pin or generated-artifact changes are
present. I independently ran all 77 loop tests successfully. The reported 18
static prechecks are local checks, not CI; Lean-dependent gates are intentionally
deferred to CI under the repository policy for this Python/documentation change.
No provider mutation was performed. Three publication/identity findings remain.

scripts/loop_engine.py:650 — blocker (BR-1)
  Recovery identity compares the repository spelling case-sensitively, and line
  1427 hashes that spelling into a new registry filename. GitHub repository names
  are case-insensitive (the publication remote check itself normalizes them).
  Reproduced using RecoveryCliTests' temporary Git fixture: initialize, reserve
  one round, uppercase spec.repository, then initialize with --state-dir
  .fresh-ledgers. Initialization succeeds and two registry records exist; the
  second ledger has zero rounds for the same issue/objective. This defeats the
  promised no-renaming reset boundary without editing Git metadata. Normalize
  repository identity consistently for registration, lookup and legacy bypass
  checks, and reject conflicting existing canonical records. Add a regression
  covering case-only aliases with a changed state path and legacy manifest.

scripts/loop_engine.py:2131 — blocker (BR-2)
  PR creation binds only the local HEAD to the passing review. The eventual
  command at lines 2163-2164 selects a remote branch name, and no remote-head
  query occurs before creation. A stale or concurrently advanced remote branch
  can therefore publish an unreviewed SHA even while local HEAD is exactly the
  reviewed SHA. Check the exact remote head before creation, then inspect the
  created PR's head and identity as a postcondition. The branch-name endpoint is
  not a compare-and-swap operation: if a race is detected, report the created PR
  truthfully and fail closed for subsequent transitions rather than claiming
  publication success. Add a stale-remote regression and a raced-result test.

scripts/loop_engine.py:1869 — blocker (BR-3)
  Issue closure calls recovery_publication_state but discards the reviewed
  ledger; its merged-PR query requests only state, mergedAt and
  closingIssuesReferences. Any merged PR that names the issue can satisfy this
  action, even when its head is not the reviewed recovery commit. Confirmed with
  a read-only mocked-provider probe: a publication ledger at a*40 and a merged PR
  at b*40 produce DRY-RUN gh issue close and return 0. Bind recovery closure to
  the exact reviewed head, expected issue branch and authorized base, with the
  relevant scope check; retain legacy semantics outside recovery mode. Add a
  negative test for a merged unrelated/unreviewed PR and a positive exact-head
  test. Explicit non-PR closure authority should remain separately considered.

Inherited formal findings for this new implementation chunk: none before C1.
These three findings must remain in the next panel's inherited review corpus.

# C1 abstraction review

Reviewed the frozen implementation and OpenSpec change against base
`b8306d6b9775d34fdbbb4504f639fe98085efd38`. Untracked handoff and observation
files are not included in this verdict.

Findings: 0. Lifts: 0. Inherited findings for this implementation panel: none.
Resolution map: `{}`.

## Ownership and abstraction assessment

- `scripts/loop_recovery.py` owns policy normalization, recovery validation,
  immutable contract/snapshot projections, finding identities, aggregate budget
  accounting, plan acceptance, transitions and next-action derivation. Its
  standard-library-only dependency direction is appropriate: it neither reads
  Git nor grants provider authority.
- `scripts/loop_engine.py` remains the integration owner. Registry lookup and
  validation, locking, atomic persistence, historical byte-digest checks, CLI
  dispatch and publication binding are adapters to the existing ledger, not a
  competing controller. The shared registry is explicitly authoritative; the
  worktree ledger is a recoverable exported cache. Cache edits therefore do not
  establish a second source of truth.
- Research plans are operational evidence records, not empty mathematical
  carriers or assertions that their own conclusions have been proved. A plan
  review authorizes only `resume`. Publication separately requires an active,
  passing, full same-commit panel and complete inherited-finding dispositions.
- Negative review messages are preserved whole under deterministic identities.
  Resume archives the existing attempt instead of rewriting it. The preserved
  contract, cumulative allocation accounting and independent exact-plan review
  avoid giving successor attempts a distinct acceptance root.

## Sufficient assumptions and limits

The pure transitions require a valid recovery envelope and their declared
phase/budget preconditions. No Git checkout or provider account is imposed on
that layer. The filesystem adapter requires a local Git repository for shared
worktree identity and locking; that requirement is used, not an accidental
restriction on the pure state machine. One issue and one frozen chunk is an
explicit policy boundary for one cumulative objective, not a claim that all
future multi-issue orchestration must use this representation.

Evidence strings and distinct reviewer identity strings are supplied evidence,
not proofs of semantic resolution or cognitive independence. The design and
guidance state this boundary and assign substantive assessment to independent
reviewers. Historical records preserve their original contracts and transcripts;
the declared inventory and independent investigation remain responsible for
establishing that an adoption is complete. No hidden inference promotes research
acceptance into code acceptance.

No Lean declaration, public structure, typeclass, quotient, theorem hypothesis,
instance or import is introduced or changed. Consequently the mathematical
Lift/Carrier-with-content/Empty-carrier classification is not applicable, and
there is no Mathlib-owner novelty claim or relevant Mathlib path to search.
The new Python APIs carry implemented transitions and regression tests rather
than a speculative framework. Existing local tests are supporting evidence,
not a claim of CI completion.

# C2 abstraction review

Reviewed frozen commit `75a17ec11b1b661e97d5dbd82024845048c9bcc4` against
base `b8306d6b9775d34fdbbb4504f639fe98085efd38`, including the original
implementation, all C1 review messages, and the C2 corrections. Uncommitted
handoff changes are excluded. No code or provider mutation was performed.

## Inherited finding dispositions

- C1 BR-1: resolved. Registry filenames and repository identity comparisons now
  use casefolded repository names, including legacy-manifest bypass checks.
  The case-alias regression covers changing the state path after allocation.
- C1 BR-2: resolved. PR creation now reads the exact remote branch head before
  the write and validates the resulting PR's head, identity, base and scope.
  A detected race reports the created URL without asserting success. Separate
  subsequent publication gates still recheck the current binding.
- C1 BR-3: resolved. Recovery closure retains the reviewed ledger, requires a
  merged PR, and checks its reviewed head, issue identity, authorized base and
  frozen scope. Negative unrelated-head/branch/base/body and positive exact-head
  regression cases are present.
- C1 mathematics/style verdict-vocabulary finding: resolved. The supervisor
  and style reviewer now enumerate controller tokens and explicitly prohibit
  MERGE in recovery trailers. They no longer claim a nonexistent translation.
- C1 abstraction had no findings.

## New finding

`scripts/loop_recovery.py:156` and
`scripts/loop_engine.py:1964` — should-fix (AB-1)

Recovery preserves negative transcripts but drops the *obligation* associated
with an archived `pass_with_lift` review. `inherited_findings` excludes every
passing verdict, while `authorized_lift_targets` inspects only active-attempt
rounds. An interrupted or failed panel need never reach the passing
adjudication that checks the generalization backlog. After `resume`, a final
plain PASS neither carries that lift in its disposition corpus nor checks its
backlog entry. The full message remains in an ignored snapshot, but the active
acceptance interface has forgotten it. This contradicts the abstraction
protocol's requirement that deferred lifts not silently disappear.

A read-only in-memory probe using this commit's regression fixture confirms:
reserve a partial panel with the abstraction reviewer returning PASS_WITH_LIFT
for `foundation/General.lean` under declared prefix `foundation`; abandon the
panel; accept a recovery plan; resume; supply four plain PASS reviews with empty
resolutions. Before abandonment the authorized lift prefix is `['foundation']`;
the inherited corpus is `{}`; after resume the prefix is `[]`; the final state
passes `require_publishable`. No backlog existence was required. The lost
authority also rejects a legitimate previously authorized foundation edit after
resume, independently of the dropped deferral obligation.

Minimal correction: distinguish passing code verdicts from outstanding review
obligations. Carry lift transcripts into the inherited disposition corpus and
retain reviewer-requested lift authorization across archived attempts, bounded
by the *current original* manifest's declared canonical lift prefixes. Imported
history must not expand those prefixes. Every carried lift needs independently
assessed implementation/discharge evidence or a durable backlog disposition
before final publication; preserving a transcript alone is not that
disposition. Add partial-panel recovery and failed-panel recovery regressions,
including a historical lift outside current declared authority. Do not make a
valid deferred lift demand implementation outside the frozen scope.

## Ownership and limits

The pure recovery module remains the canonical transition/accounting owner;
the controller remains the persistence, scope and provider adapter. No duplicate
Lean carrier, theorem hypothesis, namespace, instance or import is introduced.
Mathlib searches and the mathematical Lift/Carrier/Empty-carrier classification
are inapplicable: this is a Python protocol finding, not a novelty claim about
a mathematical API. Its sufficient assumptions are an ordinarily valid partial
review, an accepted recovery plan and a subsequent passing panel; no malicious
registry mutation is needed. This is not a CI verdict.

Findings: 0 blockers, 1 should-fix. Mathematical lifts: 0.

`test_carried_lift_requires_durable_backlog_before_publication` demonstrates

finding requires only a local uncommitted backlog entry and an existing reviewed

belongs to independent reviewers; binding the evidence file to the reviewed
Git object is the mechanical durability boundary.

# Recovery research: bind supporting evidence to its immutable source

Status: proposed recovery plan, **not independently accepted**. Researcher:
`recovery_guidance`. No implementation or provider mutation was performed.
Research target: terminal initial attempt at
`43460a10c42dc092dd911768ada3f132967bc3d0`, against original base
`b8306d6b9775d34fdbbb4504f639fe98085efd38`.

## Evidence and root cause

Read the original proposal, design, tasks and six requirements, and all twelve
verbatim C1/C2/C3 review messages in `.loop-runs/automatic-recovery-review/`.
The negative corpus is C1 boundary/mathematics/style, C2 abstraction, and C3
abstraction/boundary/style. Preserve every complete transcript, including
already-resolved findings, rather than reducing it to the final BR-4 summary.
The C3 style file arrived during research; the earlier eleven-file inventory
was incomplete, not evidence that its review had passed or could be skipped.

C3 repaired obligation inheritance, but reused `backlog_records`, which reads
the current worktree (`scripts/loop_engine.py:1512–1527`). The predicate answers
whether local text mentions a target, not whether the reviewed artifact carries
its disposition. `require_recovery_lift_backlog` invokes that predicate both at
passing adjudication and publication. SHA checks separately bind the code, so
combining the two true predicates does not bind this supporting text to that
SHA. This is a missing evidence-source invariant, not a need for more review
roles or a remote attestation service.

An isolated temporary Git fixture reproduced the following without touching
repository source or contacting GitHub. The fixture used `RecoveryCliTests`
setup and `RecoveryTests.lift_recovery`, gave the successor the fixture's real
HEAD, and retained all inherited findings. Registry lookup/load were isolated
with fixture state; real Git handled the repository and remote lookup.

| Probe | Observed at C3 |
| --- | --- |
| `git show <reviewed-sha>:docs/architecture/generalization-backlog.md` before creating the file | Exit 128: artifact absent |
| Recovery backlog gate with no local entry | Rejected |
| Write target only into an untracked backlog; call the same gate | Accepted |
| Call common recovery publication gate with that state and real Git remote lookup | Accepted |
| Commit backlog at a later HEAD; retain the older reviewed SHA | Backlog gate accepted |
| Replace only the tested backlog gate's candidate SHA with nonexistent `f` repeated 40 times | Backlog gate accepted without consulting object existence |
| Modify an OpenSpec artifact without committing it | `openspec_digest` changes despite its docstring saying “committed” |

The nonexistent-object probe tests the backlog helper, not the entire publication
pipeline. Recording a normal recovery review already uses `cat-file -e`; the
new artifact helper must independently fail closed when its object is absent.
The current positive regression at `test_loop_recovery.py:620` writes an
uncommitted backlog, uses a synthetic review SHA and mocks Git wholesale. It
therefore rewards the weaker property and cannot catch the reported failure.

## Inventory of filesystem evidence

| Input | Present source/binding | Required treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lift backlog | Worktree read plus substring match | Published disposition is read from the exact candidate/reviewed Git blob; no worktree fallback |
| OpenSpec artifacts | Worktree content digest checked against registered digest on load | Frozen authority is content-bound already; accurately describe this as a content digest, not proof of a committed file. Preserve mismatch rejection |
| Execution manifest | Parsed canonical digest, registered path and contract checks | Preserve the original registered authority. Dirty semantic changes must fail; a published-plan claim needs separate Git evidence, not an inference from its pathname |
| Review input files | Read once, copied verbatim with digest into canonical ledger; final SHA trailer validated | Later file edits must not change recorded evidence. Continue using stored bytes, never reread `finding_source` as authority |
| Resolution JSON and recovery plan/review JSON | Parsed once, stored in canonical state; plan review binds submitted digest | Preserve snapshot ownership and exact plan binding; evidence adequacy remains independent reviewer judgment |
| Historical ledger files | Raw file hash checked on import, snapshot and digest retained | Preserve exact imported bytes/provenance and charged rounds; subsequent source changes cannot refresh the imported snapshot |
| Registry and exported ledger | Shared registry owns state; export is cache | Keep canonical validation/locking; exported edits cannot supply proof |
| PR body file | Validated local content, subsequently consumed by `gh --body-file` | This is outgoing intent, not reviewed backlog proof. Existing recovery PR postcheck validates actual remote body/head and reports races; retain those checks rather than claim atomicity |

The narrow fix is not “make every input a Git blob.” Review transcripts and
research plans are correctly immutable ledger snapshots. Separate the two
evidence classes: frozen authority/transcripts use stored content bindings;
claims about what will ship use Git objects selected by the review SHA. No new
carrier, service, or duplicate ledger is needed.

## Proposed recovery strategy

1. Introduce one controller-side immutable text-artifact reader taking an
   explicit full commit SHA and fixed repository-relative path. Verify that the
   object is a commit and the entry is an ordinary tracked blob; reject absent
   objects, missing paths, symlinks and non-text evidence. Never use HEAD or a
   worktree fallback. Keep Git access out of the pure recovery state machine.
2. Route **both** recovery passing-adjudication and common publication lift
   checks through that reader at `latest_round(state).commit`. Also ensure the
   subsequent generic `pass_with_lift` adjudication branch cannot fall back to
   mutable text for recovery mode. Read once per decision and reuse the bytes.
   Legacy behavior outside recovery remains unchanged unless independently
   reviewed as part of the original acceptance requirements.
3. Preserve C3's whole inherited lift transcripts, per-review resolutions and
   current-manifest prefix intersection. Historical requests outside current
   scope remain obligations to record; they never authorize out-of-scope edits.
   Prepare backlog dispositions before freezing a candidate. A later backlog
   commit needs the next allocated review round, not an unreviewed exception.
4. Distinguish binding from semantics. Replace recovery's inherited substring
   predicate with a narrow structured row check: an actual visible row outside
   code fences must have an exact `proposed ancestor` value and the existing
   required row fields, including a recognized state. Ignore the fenced schema
   example and reject prose/prefix-only matches. Define accepted optional
   backtick quoting explicitly. Independent review still judges rationale and
   substantive adequacy. Do not import the unpublished #1458 parser redesign
   or create new side-artifact publication authority.
   Leave the legacy helper unchanged outside recovery mode. Document recovery
   rows as using the canonical repository-relative target path exactly in
   `proposed ancestor`; existing namespace names or multi-line descriptive
   ancestor values are not silently coerced to paths. Such existing rows remain
   historical context and cannot satisfy a new path-specific recovery claim
   unless a complete exact-path disposition is recorded in the reviewed tree.
5. Correct the “live backlog gate,” “committed OpenSpec digest,” and “missing
   reviewer round is void” descriptions. Their observed implementations differ
   from those claims. Document which artifact owns each fact. Retain all prior
   case-normalization, provider SHA/identity checks and unchanged review grammar.

## Verification matrix for independent acceptance

Use real temporary Git repositories and real commit objects for evidence tests;
mock provider reads/writes only at the provider boundary. No positive case may
mock away the exact Git-artifact reader it is supposed to test.

| Case | Expected result |
| --- | --- |
| Reviewed commit contains the required backlog row | Adjudication and publication succeed, subject to other gates |
| Entry exists only untracked or dirty | Both decisions reject |
| Entry exists at later HEAD but not reviewed SHA | Reject |
| Reviewed SHA has entry; worktree deletes/modifies it or HEAD moves | Artifact result remains determined by reviewed SHA; push/create retain their separate HEAD/cleanliness restrictions |
| Commit, file or ordinary blob absent; path is symlink | Reject, without fallback |
| Remote PR head differs from reviewed SHA | Existing approve/attest/merge/close gates reject before mutation |
| Existing remote PR matches reviewed SHA but local dirty text alone supplies row | Common publication gate rejects for approve, attest, merge and close |
| Local push/create HEAD differs; remote branch changes during create | Retain current prechecks and truthful raced-result reporting |
| Fresh current-panel lift plus earlier PASS reviews | No retrospective finding IDs required; committed row required before passing |
| Partial/failed/imported lift carried through resume | Same finding retained and committed disposition checked |
| Historical lift outside current declared prefix | No new edit authority; disposition obligation retained |
| Prose/prefix-only ancestor mention, fenced schema/example, malformed row/state | Reject; exact visible complete row accepts |
| Fresh lift discovered after freeze, with no existing row | Append row, commit and allocate another panel; old SHA remains nonpublishable and all prior verdicts remain unchanged |
| Review source file changed after recording | Canonical transcript/digest stays unchanged |
| Manifest/OpenSpec semantic content changes after registration | Existing registered-contract checks reject; restoring original content does not replenish rounds |
| All existing loop regressions | Pass; update the misleading dirty-backlog positive test rather than preserve its expectation |

## Recovery admission and bounded continuation

The task checklist says “Max three formal panels,” and the migration paragraph
says three rounds “for this implementation.” Read alone, those phrases are
ambiguous between an initial attempt and the entire objective. The same design
and normative requirement explicitly say three rounds **per attempt** followed
by bounded research, and the user explicitly requested and authorized implementing
automatic recovery after exhaustion without another approval. Thus the initial
attempt remains terminal after C3; a successor can be admitted only by applying
that approved evidence-gated recovery policy, not by silently calling a fourth
panel or changing the task identity. This is an interpretation for independent
review, not the researcher's self-granted authorization.

Adopt a stable manual bootstrap objective `automatic-loop-recovery-core`, with
the exact original file list and acceptance, three already allocated rounds,
at most two recovery episodes, nine total allocated implementation rounds, two
plan submissions per episode, and the approved finite elapsed allowance.
The external `.loop-runs/automatic-recovery-review/objective.json` already
records this manual adoption, three allocated rounds, episode 1 researching,
and an elapsed-budget start of `2026-09-22T16:41:19-04:00` from C1. I verified
its twelve stored texts and SHA-256 hashes against the original review files.
Retain that start and derive the one-week deadline rather than restart the clock.
Research and code
subtasks share those limits; neither gets a new budget. Preserve all C1/C2/C3
commits and transcripts unchanged. No real GitHub issue number has been allocated
for this feature by this research; do not invent one to satisfy a candidate CLI.

The controller under review cannot certify its own authority. The bootstrap
supervisor should maintain an auditable declarative record with hashes of this
plan, the original contract, all twelve review files and its independent plan
review. The candidate engine can be exercised in isolated tests, but must not
authorize its own publication or silently create a canonical production registry
entry. A reviewer distinct from both researcher and implementer must accept the
exact proposed plan and this scope/authority interpretation before source edits.
If rejected, revise research within the same episode's plan allowance. If
accepted, successor code still requires all four independent roles on the same
commit, full inherited dispositions and existing publication permissions.

This report grants no acceptance and no publication authority. New base commits
or other concurrently modified worktrees do not alter the frozen attempt; do
not rebase or merge them as an uncounted repair. If the independent reviewer
cannot reconstruct standing authority for this adoption, report that concrete
authority gap rather than inventing approval. Otherwise execute the already
authorized research/review/resume transitions automatically.

review.assessment: Independently verified the exact research-plan hash and all twelve original review texts/hashes/trailers. The plan preserves seven complete negative transcripts, original scope and all six acceptance requirements. Its eight-input evidence-source inventory, single immutable Git-blob adapter, both adjudication-path checks, structured exact-target backlog predicate and real-Git negative/positive matrix are a substantive changed strategy for BR-4/residual AB-1, not an ordinary fourth repair round. Standing user authority supports explicit external bootstrap adoption despite conflicting original implementation-wide three-panel wording; retain that wording by original commit and record the adoption rather than erase it. Before source revision, persist this submission and review, preserve the three failed allocations and full contract/history, and admit attempt 2 within three panels per attempt, nine total, two episodes, two submissions each and the fixed elapsed deadline. The next panel is aggregate allocation 4. The C1 timestamp is a formal-review-era anchor, not proof that earlier execution time was zero; never advance it at resume. This acceptance is independent of researcher and implementer and admits only the bounded successor plan, not code acceptance or provider mutation. Four independent reviewers must still assess the entire frozen successor candidate and all inherited findings. See admission-audit.md for complete evidence, conditions and rejection boundaries.

# Independent recovery-admission audit

Auditor: `/root/recovery_admission_audit`. This agent did not implement the
controller or author the recovery research plan. This is an authority/history
audit, not acceptance of a plan or a passing implementation review.

## Decision

**Conditionally admit an intermediate research episode; do not yet admit a
successor implementation attempt.** Applying the user's requested recovery
policy to this implementation can be justified, but it must be an explicit
external bootstrap adoption, not a claim that the three-panel implementation
contract always permitted a fourth panel.

The user expressly requested autonomous intermediate research when adversary
rounds cannot finish, while rejecting a blind cap bypass, and then requested
implementation of that recommendation. This supplies authority for bounded
research and independently accepted recovery without another routine approval.
It does not supply publication acceptance or unlimited attempts. The feature's
own new code and edited AGENTS instructions are not independent authority for
their own acceptance.

The original task and migration text genuinely say "Max three formal panels"
and "at most three review/improve rounds for this implementation." That is
narrower than the proposal/specification's per-attempt recovery policy. It is
not sound to erase or silently reinterpret those sentences after failure.
Preserve that original contract and explicitly document this policy adoption
and ambiguity. The first attempt remains terminal under its original cap.
Only the user's overarching recovery instruction, independently assessed here,
supports considering a separately admitted successor under cumulative limits.

## Evidence checked

- Read the user request in the inherited conversation, all current proposal,
  design, specification and task artifacts, and the task artifact at original
  frozen commit `d1ab5554e18b664bf7713b3350042470d691e537`.
- Inspected `objective.json` and its embedded verbatim review history,
  particularly the terminal BR-4 / residual AB-1 finding. This finding is real
  committed-evidence binding work, not merely a reviewer's missing response.
- Independently checked all 12 stored review texts against their source files,
  raw SHA-256 hashes, full frozen-commit/verdict trailers and four-role quorum.
  All matched. The three frozen commits are `d1ab5554e18b664bf7713b3350042470d691e537`,
  `75a17ec11b1b661e97d5dbd82024845048c9bcc4`, and
  `43460a10c42dc092dd911768ada3f132967bc3d0`; all three panels require changes.
- The audited objective snapshot SHA-256 is
  `ded86e8a24fd107e9f6c758824c4eb357a7471a56a6bf80f8ab755dea10ae952`.
  This binds this audit to the snapshot examined; it is not a signature or
  authorization for subsequent unexamined edits.
- The configured start timestamp is the original candidate's Git commit time,
  not necessarily the beginning of implementation/research. No earlier elapsed
  work may be silently omitted when describing the time budget.

## Mandatory admission conditions

1. Preserve the initial attempt, its three allocations, original contract,
   every verbatim review and terminal failure. Do not change old verdicts,
   relabel C3 as incomplete, open a C4, or reset identity/scope/file-list under a
   replacement chunk. The one objective remains `automatic-loop-recovery-core`.
2. Make the external bootstrap adoption explicit in the research/admission
   record and subsequent planning clarification. Preserve original text by
   commit/digest and call out the conflicting implementation-wide wording.
   Clarification must not weaken any of the six acceptance requirements or
   remove deferred lift durability, scope bounds, independent review, or any
   outstanding finding. This audit does not itself edit those artifacts.
3. Research before code revision. The plan must explain why the earlier method
   missed this boundary, inspect all acceptance-critical evidence reads, give
   concrete reproduction evidence, propose a meaningfully improved verification
   strategy and list executable adversarial checks. "Apply BR-4 and retry" with
   no broader read-model examination is insufficient evidence of recovery.
4. Bind independent plan acceptance to the exact plan digest and full inherited
   corpus, including complete negative C3 transcripts and prior lift obligations.
   Its reviewer must be distinct from the implementer and plan author. This
   audit is not that acceptance; no plan has been examined or accepted here.
5. Externally account for at most three panels per successor, nine aggregate
   allocations including the three already spent, two recovery episodes and
   two plan submissions per episode, with one fixed elapsed deadline. Charge
   partial allocations and rejected plan submissions before redispatch. Preserve
   research effort in the same objective. Use an honestly documented original
   start (or explicitly conservative bound), never reset the clock at resume.

I would reject admission if the original "three panels" wording were rewritten
without provenance, if a code revision preceded independent exact-plan
acceptance, if the research merely renamed the same ordinary repair round, if
history or obligations were dropped, or if an implementer/self-controller
claimed its own acceptance. These are substantive boundaries, not requests for
another routine user confirmation.
